translationRepairs: Ha Panlong, Guo Xing, Ren Ju, Ye Daxiong, Ma Liangzhu, Ben Jinzhong, and Liu Shun
Ha Panlong, his son Guo Xing, Ren Ju, Ye Daxiong, Ma Liangzhu, Ben Jinzhong, and Liu Shun
s0002 reads 哈攀龍子國興; 子 marks Guo Xing as Ha Panlong's son, which the idiomatic listing omits.
Chieftain Nuo'erta, with their ruler Mengbo dead, sent the envoy Deluyun to ask for a withdrawal.
Chieftain Nuo'erta, on the orders of their ruler Mengbo, sent the envoy Deluyun to ask for a withdrawal.
以其酋懵駁命 is 'by order of their ruler Mengbo' (命 = command); the idiomatic wrongly makes Mengbo dead.
The chieftain Nuo'erta, because their ruler Mengbo had been killed, sent an envoy named Deluyun to the army to beg that troops be withdrawn.
The chieftain Nuo'erta, by order of their ruler Mengbo, sent an envoy named Deluyun to the army to beg that troops be withdrawn.
The same 命 is Mengbo's order, not his death; the literal 'had been killed' invents a killing absent from the Chinese.

Guo Xing took a detour through Akemuya Ravine toward Ma'erdike stockade; finding Cebudan's forests too deep and paths too narrow for a main column, he left two thousand men with Hailancha to assault Ma'erdike.

Guo Xing took a detour through Akemuya Ravine toward Ma'erdike stockade; finding Cebudan's forests too deep and paths too narrow for a main column, he led two thousand men to assist Hailancha in assaulting Ma'erdike.
乃將二千人佐海蘭察 means Guo Xing led two thousand men to assist Hailancha; 'left … with Hailancha' reverses the agency of 將 and 佐.
In year twelve he was ordered to Jinchuan under Governor Zhang Guangsi.
In Qianlong 12 (1747), he was ordered to campaign against Jinchuan under Governor-General Zhang Guangsi.
命徵金川 orders a campaign against Jinchuan, while 總督 is Governor-General; naming Qianlong 12 (1747) follows the biography's dating context.
Now, employing Ju and the others separately — none of them served in the Zhandui campaign and have no restraints — they should be encouraged to press forward boldly.
Now, employing Ju and the others separately — none of them served in the Zhandui campaign and they have no restraints — they should be encouraged to press forward boldly.
After 'none of them served…', the second verb needs an explicit subject; bare 'and have' is ungrammatical English.

At that time the emperor had just ordered Ju's formal appointment; Commissioner-General and Grand Secretary Neqin reported Ju's death in service; the emperor, reading the memorial, wept and also issued an edict: "Ju, stirred by loyal indignation, welcomed death as though it were sweet; yet I, on account of petty rebels rampaging, sent a worthy minister into peril — the thought cuts deeply!

At that time the emperor had just ordered Ju's formal appointment; Commissioner-General and Grand Secretary Neqin reported Ju's death in service; the emperor, reading the memorial, wept and also issued an edict: "Ju, stirred by loyal indignation, welcomed death as though it were sweet; yet I, on account of petty rebels rampaging, sent a worthy minister into peril — the thought cuts deeply!"
Chinese closes the edict with ！」; the literal opens the quotation but never closes it.
Summoned to court, he had his son Jijun appointed an imperial guardsman with the blue arrow feather and ordered to escort Daxiong to his new command.
Daxiong entered court for an audience. His son Jijun was appointed an imperial guardsman with the blue arrow feather and ordered to escort Daxiong to his new command.
官其子 is an imperial grant to Daxiong's son; naming Daxiong explicitly avoids the proposal's dangling modifier and preserves the subject of 入覲.
Jijun went to Changde to fetch the family; en route he borrowed money from the local people, and Daxiong reported it.
Jijun went to Changde to fetch the family; en route he borrowed money from Hui people, and Daxiong reported it.
假回民金 names Hui people (回民) as the lenders; 'local people' erases that ethnoreligious marker.
Jijun reached Changde to meet the family; on the way he borrowed money from the people; Daxiong reported this.
Jijun reached Changde to meet the family; on the way he borrowed money from Hui people; Daxiong reported this.
Literal likewise drops 回民; restoring 'Hui people' matches the Chinese.
Liangzhu asked to shift the Rongbu column to the rescue; Governor Zhang Guangsi refused, and Xing was lost to the enemy.
Liangzhu asked to move the Rongbu column to the rescue; Governor-General Zhang Guangsi refused, and Zhang Xing fell into the rebels' hands.
總督 is Governor-General, and 興 refers to Zhang Xing; naming him removes an otherwise ambiguous one-word reference.

In year thirty he followed General Ming Rui against Burma, attacked Manjie, took sixteen wooden palisades, killed three rebels, was wounded in the forehead, and fought again the next day still bandaged.

In the thirtieth year of Qianlong (1765) he followed General Ming Rui against Burma, attacked Manjie, took sixteen wooden palisades, killed three rebels, was wounded in the forehead, and fought again the next day still bandaged.
In this biography's Qianlong-era sequence, 三十年 is Qianlong 30 (1765); clarifying the reign and western year matches the chapter's conversion practice and the Chinese year.
Knowing Shun's knowledge of the frontier, the emperor transferred him to regional commander of Xining in Gansu.
Because Shun was familiar with frontier conditions, the emperor transferred him to regional commander of Xining in Gansu.
上以順熟邊情 is a causal 以-clause (because Shun knew frontier conditions); 'Knowing Shun's knowledge' is broken English that obscures that cause.
